overview.text: The document system brings submitting, reviewing, signing and numbering into one place. Everyone sees the same status and gets notified as soon as a document moves to the next stage.

rows: Applicants couldn't tell where their document was and had to come and ask
Every document gets a reference ID, status can be checked online anytime, and an email arrives at every change

overview.text: What the system is made of
Most people only ever use the website; everything else runs in the background. A rough idea is enough.

head: Part
Think of it as
What it does
rows: Submitting, checking status, and the staff work queues
Submit, send a review result, upload a signed file — for files over 3 MB or when the website is down
Holds every document, the staff list, and the document number register
Creates reference IDs, files documents, sets access, issues numbers, sends email and LINE
Stores every PDF, in folders by organization

overview.text: Every channel writes to the same register, so submitting through the website or the form gives the same result.

overview.text: How a document travels

Every document passes three stages — applicant → secretary → president — and ends as “Approved” (with a document number) or “Rejected” (fix it and submit again). The example below follows the Music Club's “ขออนุมัติจัดกิจกรรมรับน้องใหม่” (freshmen welcome activity request).

overview.caption: Read from the top left: the document goes down to the secretary. If it fails it goes back up to the applicant; if it passes it goes down to the president, then the system issues a number and tells the applicant.

overview.text: Stage 1 — The applicant submits (status: Pending review)
Fill in the form, attach the PDF and send. The screen shows a reference ID such as `TRK-20261011-001`. The system then:

items: Files the PDF in the organization's folder as `ชมรมดนตรี_ขออนุมัติจัดกิจกรรมรับน้องใหม่.pdf` (organization_document name)
Makes the file open only for the applicant and staff
Emails a confirmation to the applicant and alerts the secretary by email and LINE

overview.text: These happen in the background, so they may follow a few minutes after the success screen. Until then the file link shows “Preparing file”.

overview.alt: Submission success screen with the reference ID
The confirmation email the applicant receives
overview.caption: System emails are sent in Thai

overview.text: Stage 2 — The secretary reviews (status: Awaiting signature or Rejected)
The secretary opens **Pending Review**, reads the file, and picks one of two paths:

items: **Send to President** → status becomes “Awaiting signature”, the file is renamed `…_ส่งเซ็น.pdf` (sent for signing), and the president is emailed
**Reject** → type a reason (a marked-up file can be attached); the applicant gets an email with a pre-filled resubmission link

overview.text: Stage 3 — The president signs (status: Approved)
The president opens the file from the email, signs it outside the system, then uploads the signed file on **Pending Signature**. The system:

items: Checks that the uploader may sign and that the document is “Awaiting signature”
Issues a document number such as `EGSA 012/2569` and records it in the register
Keeps the signed file and makes a number-stamped copy for the register
Emails the applicant the document number and a link to the signed file

overview.alt: Approval email to the applicant with the document number
overview.caption: System emails are sent in Thai

overview.text: Documents move only in order and can't skip a stage. An approved document can't be rejected afterwards, and a rejected one must be submitted again (it gets a new reference ID, but the system remembers which one it came from).

overview.text: Emails go out from a background queue and normally arrive within a few minutes. If you can't find one, check Spam first.
Document numbers and file versions
Document numbers look like `EGSA 012/2569`: the EGSA prefix, a 3-digit running number, and the Buddhist Era year.

items: Numbers are issued **only on approval**, so they follow the order of approval, not of submission
Numbering restarts at 001 every calendar year
Simultaneous approvals never share a number, and a document can't be approved twice

overview.text: Contact
Common questions are answered on the [FAQ](/faq) page. For a problem, email [muegsamo@gmail.com](mailto:muegsamo@gmail.com) with the document's reference ID.

tour.text: The menu depends on the email you sign in with. Staff see every applicant menu plus extra menus for their role.
Every page has a **ไทย / EN** language switch. On a phone, the left menu hides behind the ☰ button at the top left.
A Sign in with Google button plus shortcuts to submit or check status without signing in. Below are the three stages of the process (pictured in the Overview tab).
Enter the reference ID plus the email or phone number used to submit, to see one document's status (pictured in the Applicants tab).
Explains what is collected, why, and who can see it. Linked at the bottom of every page.
Counts your documents by status (pending review / awaiting signature / approved) and lists anything to follow up, such as rejections.
Starts with a steps page, then the form (how to fill it in is in the Applicants tab).

tour.alt: The steps page shown before the form

tour.text: Once signed in you only need the reference ID — no need to confirm your email again.
Every document submitted with this email. Click one to see its timeline, reviewer, signer, document number, and the signed file.
Save your name, student ID and phone so the submit form fills them in next time. The email can't be changed — it comes from the Google account you signed in with.
Answers to common applicant questions such as timing, files that won't open, and resubmitting.
Counts every document in the system by status and lists what's waiting for you. Click “View all in queue” to carry on.
The main workspace: every document “Pending review”, searchable and filterable by organization. Each card has “Send to President” and “Reject” (pictured in the Overview tab).
Documents in every status, with a monthly summary, search, and filters by status or month (pictured in the Secretary tab).
Every document number issued, with the date, title, sender and approver.
A quick reference: status meanings, short steps for each role, and staff FAQs.
Like the secretary's, but the waiting list shows documents awaiting signature.

Every document “Awaiting signature”, with the reviewer's name. Each card has “Approve & Issue Document Number” (pictured in the President tab). The president also sees Document Records, Document Registry and Help, like the secretary.

items: Prepare the document as a PDF up to 3 MB, with a title that states the purpose and the activity
Fill in your details correctly — especially your email, since every result goes there
Keep the reference ID and follow the status until the document is approved
If it's rejected, fix it as asked and resubmit from the email link

applicant.caption: The dashed line is the fallback for files over 3 MB — the result is exactly the same as submitting on the website.

applicant.text: Before you start: which email to use

Files open only for the Google account matching the email you enter. Use Gmail, or an @student.mahidol.ac.th address that is [registered with the university's Google Workspace](https://muit.mahidol.ac.th/docs/users-guide/google-workspace/edu_workspace_reg_2026/). Any other email can still submit, but you won't be able to open the files yourself.

items.text: Click **Submit Document** on the home page or in the left menu (signing in with Google first lets the form fill itself next time).
Read the steps, then click **I understand, continue to submit**.
items.alt: The steps page shown before the form

items.text: Fill in your name, student ID, email, phone, and the document title.
Choose the organization type (Student Union / Club / Department / Other), then the specific unit. For “Other”, type the name yourself.
If you're resubmitting after a rejection, enter the previous reference ID (optional).
Attach the PDF, tick both boxes, and click **Submit**.
items.alt: The file field and checkboxes, filled in

items.text: Wait about half a minute while it says “Submitting…”. **You can visit other pages on the site, but don't close or refresh the tab** until it finishes.
When it's done you'll see the reference ID. If you were on another page, a notice pops up at the bottom right instead.
items.alt: Finished while on another page: the notice at the bottom right

applicant.text: A yellow box appears as soon as you pick the file. Either compress the PDF and choose it again, or click **Submit via Google Form** — it accepts up to 10 MB and is pre-filled with what you typed (you still attach the file and tick consent yourself).

applicant.alt: The file-too-large box with the Google Form button

items: **Signed out:** on **Check Status**, enter the reference ID plus the email or phone you used (so nobody can guess an ID and see your document).
**Signed in:** **My Documents** lists everything submitted with your email. Click one to see its timeline and open the file.

applicant.text: If you see “Preparing file” instead of a link, access to the file is still being set up. The page updates by itself within a few minutes.

applicant.alt: My Documents with one document's details open

applicant.text: The rejection email gives the reason, attaches a marked-up file (if any), and includes a resubmission link.

items.text: Fix the document as the email asks.
Click the resubmission link in the email — your details and the old reference ID are already filled in.
items.alt: The rejection email with the reason and resubmission link

items.text: Attach the corrected file and send — you'll get a new reference ID.

rows: The file won't open and asks you to request access
Sign out of other Google accounts and sign in with the email you submitted with. For a student email, register it with Google Workspace first
Wait a few minutes, check Spam, then check the status with your reference ID. Don't submit again yet
Your entries are kept — send again, or click “Try again” in the notice
“Your last send may not have finished”
The tab was closed while sending. Check your confirmation email or My Documents before submitting again
There's a limit per time period to stop spam. Wait a little and try again

applicant.alt: The “Sending failed” notice with its Try again button

items: **Review every document before it reaches the president**, then send it on or reject it — within the 3-working-day turnaround promised to applicants (including the president's step).
**Write clear rejection reasons**, attaching a marked-up file when you can.
**Keep the staff list** in the “เจ้าหน้าที่” (staff) tab in line with the current committee.
**Watch system alerts** in email and the LINE group, and tell the maintainer about anything unusual.
**Help applicants who can't open their files** — when that alert arrives, send them the file another way.

secretary.caption: Every queue item ends one of two ways; the routine tasks at the bottom carry on throughout your term.

items.text: Ask the maintainer or the previous secretary to add your email and role to the staff tab (see “Add, change or remove staff”).
Open the website and click **Sign in with Google** using that exact email.
The left menu now shows **Pending Review**, **Document Records**, **Document Registry** and **Help**. If not, your email isn't in the staff tab yet.

secretary.text: Review and send to the president

items.text: Open **Pending Review** and click **Attached file → Open document** to read it.
If it's fine, click **Send to President**, then **Confirm send to president** (the reviewer is always recorded as whoever is signed in).
The card shows “In progress…” with a status box at the bottom right. You can visit other pages, but don't close the tab.
items.alt: Sending: the card says “In progress…” and the status box appears

items.text: When done, the document leaves the queue and a “Sent to president” notice appears. A red “Sending failed” box means it's still in the queue — click “Try again”.
items.alt: Done: the document leaves the queue and a notice appears

items.text: Click **Reject** on the document's card.
Type the reason (required), saying which page and what to change.
Attach a marked-up file (optional, up to 3 MB; if larger, a **Reject via Google Form** button appears, pre-filled).
items.alt: Attachment over 3 MB: the Reject via Google Form button

items.text: Click **Confirm rejection** — the applicant is emailed straight away and it **can't be undone**, so read it over first.
items.alt: The reject window with a reason and file

items: **Document Records** — every document in every status, with search, filters by status or month, and a monthly summary on top. Click a row for its timeline and files.
**Document Registry** — every document number issued, in order.

secretary.text: These two pages open the number-stamped trial copy, while applicants get the signed copy (see document numbers in the Overview tab).
The staff list lives in the Google Sheet tab **เจ้าหน้าที่** (columns: name / email / role). Valid roles are `secretary` `vice_secretary` `president` `vp_internal` `vp_external`.

items.text: Type a new email into an empty cell, or type over an existing email to replace someone.
A pop-up asks whether to grant/revoke file access right away — click **Yes**.
items.alt: The add-staff confirmation pop-up in Google Sheet

items.text: Every secretary gets an email and LINE alert that the tab changed — if it wasn't someone on the team, look into it right away.

secretary.text: Editing several cells at once, or changing a name/role, makes the system ask the maintainer to run the access sync (covered in the maintainer guide).
Working from Google Sheet when the website is down

items: **Send to president:** in the `ระบบส่งเอกสาร` tab, change that row's `สถานะ` (status) to `รอเซ็น`. The sheet asks you to confirm before emailing the president.

**Reject:** click the link in the `ลิงก์ส่งผลการตรวจสอบ` (review link) column. It opens the form with the reference ID filled in. Be signed in to Google with your staff email and tick “record my email” in the form.
Never edit the form-response tabs or rename column headers. Moving columns is fine.

secretary.alt: The confirmation pop-up when changing the status in the sheet

head: Alert
What to do
rows: Open the queue and review it
Send them the file another way, or suggest a Google account
Check who it was; if you don't know them, tell the maintainer
Make sure it was someone on the team
Background job failed / queue problem / backup failed

secretary.alt: The new-document LINE card in the secretary group
secretary.caption: System LINE messages are in Thai

secretary.text: Approved documents can't be rejected, and a rejection can't be undone. If you reject the wrong one, ask the applicant to resubmit and tell the maintainer.

items: **Consider and sign documents the secretary has reviewed** — approval is when the official document number is issued.
**Upload the right signed file** — it's the copy the applicant receives and uses.
**The VPs for internal and external affairs can sign** when the president is away, on the same page. The system records who actually signed.

president.caption: Both paths end in the same place: the system issues the document number and tells the applicant automatically.

president.text: The “document awaiting signature” email goes to the president, or to the vice presidents if no president email is listed.

items.text: Open the “awaiting signature” email and use the document link to download it for signing (digitally, or print–sign–scan).
items.alt: The awaiting-signature email to the president

items.text: Click the link to the signature queue and sign in with your staff email.
On the document's card, click **Approve & Issue Document Number**.
Attach the signed PDF and click **Confirm approve & issue document number** — this can't be undone.
items.alt: The approve window with the signed file attached

items.text: After about half a minute the document leaves the queue with a “Document approved” notice, and the applicant is emailed the number.
items.alt: Approved: the document leaves the queue and a notice appears

president.text: Files over 3 MB, or the website is down
Use the Google Form button that appears in the approve window, or the backup form link in the email. The reference ID and your position are already filled in.

items: Sign in to Google with your staff email before opening the form
Tick **record my email** in the form — you can't send without it
The system checks that your email matches your position; if not, nothing is approved and the secretary is alerted

president.alt: The file-too-large box with the Google Form button
